title: devx: register `scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs` in `scripts/upstream-port-pin.json` at its own ref — item 2 of objectui#8385, unblocked by objectui#8288
body:
Split out of objectui#8385 by its triage (comment 5582520495), which narrowed that card to item 1 (the prose fix, landed separately). This is item 2. objectui#8385 is not addressed here.

## Why it is possible now

objectui#8288 retired the ledger-wide `upstream.ref`. Measured on `origin/main` `da5e4f69e`:

- `scripts/upstream-port-pin.json` `upstream` carries `repo` alone — no `ref`.
- Every `files[]` entry carries its own `ref`, and `validatePin` requires it to be a 40-char sha (`scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs`, the `f.ref` / `HEX40` check).
- `validatePin` REFUSES a pin that still carries `upstream.ref`.
- `resyncedPin` writes only the re-synced entry's `ref` and digest, returning every other entry structurally untouched.
- The gate's own green line proves entries at different refs coexist today: `3 ported file(s) match ... each at its own pinned ref (2 distinct: ...)`.

So registering this file no longer forces either of the two trades the old rationale rejected (ship a weaker construct table, or drag every pinned file to one ref).

## What the work is

Not a schema change — per-file work with its own review surface:

1. read the upstream blob (`objectstack-ai/objectstack`) at the ref this port was taken from;
2. compute its SHA-256 for `upstreamSha256`;
3. declare every divergence as an exact `upstream`/`ported` text pair with a `why` of at least 10 characters — `validatePin` enforces all of that, and each declared snippet must match exactly once.

The port has diverged from upstream in at least the shebang-census half (this repo measures 0 shebang-only scripts where upstream calls that half load-bearing), so the divergence list is real work, not a formality.

## Why it matters

`scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs` has NO drift gate — its own docblock says so. Upstream actively sweeps the construct table; improvements arrive here only if someone carries them by hand, and a construct missing from `CONSTRUCTS` reads as an approval, which is the exact failure class this gate exists to catch.

`scripts/**` is not governed surface (measured: `governedPathsIn(['scripts/check-bash32-floor.mjs'])` returns `[]`), so `--resync` needs no long-form flag here.

No assignee.
